suggestion: Where do market prices come from?
options: A. Licensed/commercial price feed with timestamps (costs money, clean licence) | B. Free aggregator archive pinned by commit hash (free, but not official and has no timestamp) | C. Hand-record one operator's public board three times a week (free, official-ish, slow and sparse)
recommended_path: C now, A as soon as there is budget: C proves whether the pipeline can consume a price at all, and B must not be used because an untimestamped price cannot be an opening or a closing number
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to A if a licensed feed is available inside the budget, or to B if an aggregator published opening and closing prices with timestamps
note: This is the single blocking decision. Nothing can be certified while it is open: gates G2, G3 and G4 all need a price. Note that the aggregator lines another desk holds (session 83a7d6a8) are untimestamped, so they satisfy none of the three gates either.

suggestion: How do we get starter evidence (snap counts)?
options: A. Official snap-count source if one is readable and permitted | B. Club game-day inactives articles only (32 fetches a week, gives 'did not play', not 'how much') | C. Do nothing and keep club depth charts as the only starter source
recommended_path: B next: it is official, cheap and turns 'expected starter' into 'confirmed unavailable'. A only if it is licensed cleanly
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to A if an official snap source is confirmed readable; it would fall back to C if the 32 inactives pages do not parse reliably
note: Today 0 of 145 completed games have any starter confirmation. Requirement R-10 is blocked by this choice.

options: A. Scheduled job writing to a private bucket with hashes and a freshness alarm | B. Keep them in git (already immutable and hashed) and add a scheduled commit | C. Do nothing, capture by hand each session
recommended_path: B now: git already gives immutability and a hash per capture, at zero cost. Move to A when there is a budget and an alerting target
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to A as soon as a freshness alert has somewhere to fire
note: Requirements R-29, R-39, R-54 all wait on this. The multi-day snapshot idea cannot be tested without it.

suggestion: Public analysis layer vs private data layer
options: A. Publish only derived numbers and link to the official page | B. Publish official published facts (standings, schedule, injury designations) but no derived row-level data | C. Publish everything we hold
recommended_path: A, with B for official published facts: official facts are already public on the source site, but derived rows and any licensed row-level data should not be republished until the terms are read
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to C only after the terms are read and permit it, per source
note: No terms have been read for any source. Until they are, this desk publishes official published facts plus its own derived numbers and nothing else.

suggestion: Stadium roof, surface and weather overlay
options: A. Official 90-minute roof designation plus an NWS gridpoint forecast per stadium | B. Roof designation only | C. Defer until prices exist
recommended_path: C: this feature changes totals pricing, and totals pricing cannot be evaluated until there is a market price. Building it now produces a number nobody can score
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to A the moment S-01 is decided
note: Requirements R-58. Deferred by design, not forgotten.

suggestion: Extend the official results feed backwards
options: A. Transcribe prior seasons week by week from nfl.com | B. Use an aggregator archive | C. Stay on 2026 only
recommended_path: A for 2025 first: one extra season gives a train/validation split and makes the certification sample real. B is inadmissible under the official-only rule
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to B only if the official-only rule is relaxed by decision
note: This is the cheapest route to unblocking R-70 and the sample-size gate G1. It is mechanical work, not research.

options: A. Keep both estimators visible with the gap column until a walk-forward comparison picks one | B. Collapse to the better one now | C. Average them
recommended_path: A: the brief asks for this explicitly, and with 9 remaining weeks the comparison has a real chance of being informative
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to B if the walk-forward gap stays inside its own interval for the rest of the season
decision_status: IMPLEMENTED (as a rule, pending the comparison)
note: The gap column is published on the lines page. The collapse rule is pre-registered and has not fired.

suggestion: Should the designation (Out/Questionable) be a model feature?
options: A. Yes, at face value | B. No, until the play rate per designation is measured against inactives | C. Yes, but only as a surprise (delta), never as a level
recommended_path: B now, then C: no designation enters the model this season. Once several seasons of designations and inactives exist, C is the right form
what_would_change_the_call: It would change as soon as Q-15 is answered with a measured play rate and a confidence interval
note: The ablation in R-27/R-28 is the substitute: same model with and without the personnel block, once a time series exists.

options: A. Win rate | B. Benchmark-relative Brier skill with a cluster-robust lower bound | C. Season-long ROI
recommended_path: B, with C explicitly forbidden and A shown only as descriptive context: ROI is banned by the brief and win rate cannot separate skill from variance
what_would_change_the_call: It would change only if a proper score cannot be computed, which is not the case
note: The staking board stays empty because ROI cannot be computed without prices - which is the point of the split.

options: A. Rank them on multiplied marginals | B. Rank them only with a validated joint probability and the operator's void/push rules | C. Ban them
recommended_path: B: multiplying marginals is invalid under dependence, and the joint probability is not available, so the divisions are empty rather than populated with a wrong number
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to A never; to C if the joint evidence proves unobtainable after S-01 and S-02 are decided
note: Both divisions are empty by design. This is a pass, not a failure to deliver.

suggestion: How is a strategy promoted, demoted and re-promoted?
options: A. Ad hoc judgement | B. Two stages: proper-score qualification, then prospective CLV/ROI escrow, with six demotion triggers | C. Promote on any positive sample
recommended_path: B: the demotion triggers are published with thresholds so a live family can be sent back to paper without an argument
what_would_change_the_call: It would change if a trigger proves too noisy once there are prices to test it against
note: Stage two cannot run without prices. Stage one runs and currently certifies nothing.

suggestion: Consolidate the NFL desks in this repo
options: A. Add another desk | B. Consolidate the NFL namespaces into one desk | C. Leave them and add an index that says which number is current
recommended_path: C now, B at the next integration session. Six NFL namespaces now answer this brief, three of them decision-readiness desks built on the same day, and a reader cannot tell which number is current
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to B when an integration session is scheduled
note: Namespaces visible on main as this session merged: nfl-desk-3fb93d11, nfl-desk-864d5668, nfl-desk-d38e90c5, nfl-market-desk (83a7d6a8), nfl-560ed315 and nfl-readiness-cba42531. This session publishes its own namespace and touches nothing owned by another session.

suggestion: Should venue be read from the game centre or the schedule page?
options: A. Game centre per fixture | B. The venue string nfl.com prints on the schedule page | C. Team home-stadium mapping
recommended_path: A for completeness, B is what this session used and is defensible: it is the same publisher. 1 of 13 was read from the game centre as a check
what_would_change_the_call: It would change to A once the 12 remaining game-centre reads are done (cheap, pure transcription)
note: Flagged as F-09 so the mixed provenance is visible rather than hidden.

options: A. Pin every capture to expected row counts and required fields, fail the build loudly | B. Warn only | C. Nothing
recommended_path: A: this is already how the build works - a missing field fails verification rather than publishing a blank
what_would_change_the_call: It would change only if a source legitimately changes shape, which is exactly when we want to be told
note: The verification harness fails the build on a row-count or field drift.
